service.description: Open a merge request into a target branch (the default branch when empty), as the current user: of a source branch of the same repository, by a user who may push to it; or of a branch of another repository of the target's fork network (sourceRepositoryId), by a user who may view the target and has the update right on the source: the branch is followed while that holds (sync#MergeRequestHead), and with git-server review-start-hidden such a merge request starts hidden, as one pushed for review does. A draft is not merged until it is marked ready. Its number is the repository's next from 1; its head is kept at refs/merge-requests/[mergeRequestNum]/head, and its merge base and mergeability are read now. Only one open request per source and target. Each reviewer asked for must be able to view the repository. Webhooks get a merge_request event (opened). With authorization disabled only: mergeRequestNum (a free number, for an import), and pushedForReview with headCommitId and reviewTopic (what propose#MergeRequest passes: no source branch, the commit is already in the repository). Refusals an application tells apart start with a code (docs/interfaces/Git-Hosting.md, Error codes): GitArchived, GitNoSuchRef, GitNotInNetwork, GitMergeRequestExists, GitNumberTaken.

parameter.name: sourceRef
parameter.description: The source branch; required unless pushedForReview

parameter.name: sourceRepositoryId
parameter.description: The repository of the source branch: one of the fork network of repositoryId. Empty: repositoryId

parameter.name: mergeRequestNum
parameter.description: With authorization disabled only

parameter.name: pushedForReview
parameter.description: With authorization disabled only

parameter.name: headCommitId
parameter.description: With pushedForReview: the head, a commit of the repository's store

parameter.name: hidden
parameter.description: Open it hidden (set#MergeRequestHidden), so its commits are never read before the application shows it; with authorization disabled only

service.description: Commits offered for review with no branch, by a user who may view the repository and need not push to it: what a push to refs/for/[targetRef] and a proposal of commit#GitFiles call once headCommitId is in the repository's store. Called with authorization disabled only (the caller checked view, and that the commit is the caller's own). The open merge request of the current user for the target and the topic (the one with no topic when none is given), or the one named, takes the commit as its new head, as a push to a source branch does (synchronize); when there is none a merge request is opened (create#MergeRequest, pushedForReview), titled as given, else by defaultTitle. Its head is refs/merge-requests/[mergeRequestNum]/head.

parameter.name: defaultTitle
parameter.description: The title of a new merge request when title is empty (the first commit's summary)

parameter.name: mergeRequestId
parameter.description: Update this open proposal of the user

parameter.name: hidden
parameter.description: Open a new one hidden (git-server review-start-hidden): the application shows it (set#MergeRequestHidden) once it has let its text through

service.description: Keep refs/merge-requests/[mergeRequestNum]/head of a merge request's repository at its source's head: the source branch's (of the same repository, or of sourceRepositoryId, whose objects the repository does not have are copied to it first, and whose LFS objects among the files it adds become the repository's too, through its upload check), or headCommitId for one pushed for review (a commit of the repository's store; without it the ref stays as it is). A fork's branch is followed only while the author has the update right on the fork and the source is not detached (detach#MergeRequestSource); else the head stays and sourceDetachedDate is set. For one that is merged, or closed within git-server review-ref-retention-days, a missing ref is set from its recorded head (a merge request from before these refs were kept). The ref moves without a GitUpdate: it is no branch. With authorization disabled only: for create#MergeRequest, propose#MergeRequest and sync#MergeRequest.

parameter.name: headCommitId
parameter.description: The head now; empty while the source branch is gone

parameter.name: startHidden
parameter.description: git-server review-start-hidden says a new merge request of this kind (pushed for review, or from a fork) starts hidden

service.description: A merge request from a fork's branch stops following the branch (sourceDetachedDate) and keeps the head it has: later pushes to the branch no longer reach the target repository. By a user with the delete right on the source repository (its owner), by the merge request's author, or with authorization disabled. sync#MergeRequestHead does the same by itself when the author no longer has the update right on the source, and delete#GitRepository of the source does it for every merge request that follows it. It is not undone: the author opens another merge request.

Hide a merge request's commits while the application holds its text (hiddenDate), or show them again: the head of a hidden one is not fetched (by name or by id), its commits are not read by id through the get#Git* services, and get#MergeRequest, get#MergeRequestDiff and find#MergeRequests answer for it only with authorization disabled (the application decides who sees it: its author, a moderator). It is not merged while hidden, and its webhooks are sent nothing of it; when an open one is shown they get a merge_request event (opened). The repository keeps that it has held one (GitRepository.reviewHiddenDate): from then on only its refs decide which commits are read by id. With authorization disabled, else by a user with the delete right.

A merge request for its viewers: its fields, the repository's default merge method, its reviewers (with their names, whether their approval is of the current head, and whether it counts: only approvals of users who may push count, get#MergeRequestApprovals), the head's checks, the target's branch rules and what keeps it from merging now (missing), and what the current user may do (canMerge: update on the repository). A hidden one (set#MergeRequestHidden) is answered only with authorization disabled.

parameter.name: missingList
parameter.description: Why it cannot merge now; empty when it can

service.description: Change an open or draft merge request: the title, description, target branch, draft (a draft marked ready opens), merge method and whether the source branch goes after the merge. By its author or a user with update. A new target must be a branch of the repository (GitNoSuchRef) and is checked for mergeability again. A hidden one (set#MergeRequestHidden) is changed by its author, or with authorization disabled; to anyone else there is no such merge request, here and in set#MergeRequestReviewers, submit#MergeRequestReview, close#MergeRequest, reopen#MergeRequest and get#MergeRequestApprovals.

Who reviews a merge request: replace them with userIdList, or add and remove some. A reviewer kept keeps their review; one added is requested and must be able to view the repository. Not the author. By its author or a user with update.

parameter.name: userIdList
parameter.description: Replace the reviewers with these

service.description: A review of a merge request at its current head by the current user, who may view the repository: approve, request changes or comment, with a summary. Only a user who may push (update on the repository) approves; a viewer comments or requests changes. The author does not approve their own. A reviewer not requested becomes one. Webhooks get a merge_request event (reviewed).

parameter.name: decision
parameter.description: approve, request_changes or comment

service.description: Close a merge request without merging it. By its author or a user with update.
Open a closed merge request again, when its source branch is still there and the repository is not archived; its mergeability is checked again. By its author or a user with update.

Merge an open merge request by its method (the one given, else its own, else the repository's default) once the target's branch rules are met: the approvals required (of the current head when the rule dismisses stale ones; only those of users who may push count), the required checks successful on the head, a method they allow. Needs update on the repository; refused on a conflict. What merges is the head the approvals and checks were counted for, by its id: a source that moves meanwhile is not merged, nor is a branch or tag named as that id. The target moves as any ref a service writes: the gitECA pre events (source write) see the commits the merge brings, with mergeRequestId, mergeMethodEnumId and mergeSourceCommitId, and a rule's refusal is this service's error. The request becomes merged with the target's new head; its source branch is deleted when asked (kept, with a message, when its branch rules refuse). Webhooks get a merge_request event (merged).

parameter.name: message
parameter.description: Of the merge commit or squash

parameter.name: expectedHeadCommitId
parameter.description: The head the caller read (the one whose diff and checks it showed): when the merge request's head is another now, nothing is merged and the error is GitStaleRef

parameter.name: deleteSourceBranch
parameter.description: The source branch of the same repository goes when its branch rules allow. One in another repository (a fork) goes only when the calling user holds the delete right on that repository, whether or not authorization is disabled; else it is kept, with a message

parameter.name: forceDeleteSourceBranch
parameter.description: Only with authorization disabled (ignored otherwise): delete the source branch of another repository (a fork) though the calling user holds no delete right there. For an application that decided it itself.

service.description: For a viewer of the repository, the approvals of a merge request that count toward the target's branch rules: approved (of the current head when the rules dismiss stale approvals) by a user who may push to the repository now, decided as that user. merge#MergeRequest counts the same way.

Merge requests of the repositories the current user may view, last updated first, paged: by repository, status, author, reviewer, the ones waiting for a user's review, target branch and text in the title. Each with its repository, branches, author and reviewers' names, mergeability and the head's combined check state.

parameter.name: waitingForUserId
parameter.description: Requested reviews of this user not yet given, of open requests

parameter.name: sourceRepositoryId
parameter.description: Those from this fork

parameter.name: includeHidden
parameter.description: The hidden ones too; with authorization disabled only

service.description: What a merge request changes, for review: the commits and each file's diff, as get#GitCompare gives them (the moqui-diff html and hunks of numbered lines), from its target to its source while it is open, and from its recorded merge base to its recorded head once merged or closed. For its viewers.

Read a merge request's merge base and mergeability again (a trial merge of its head into its target: the source branch's for a branch of the same repository, else its own head ref); merged when the target already holds the head. For sync#MergeRequest and the services that change a request's branches.

Bring an open merge request to its source's head as it is now (sync#MergeRequestHead: its head ref follows a source branch, of its repository or of a fork): a new head is recorded, its approvals set back to requested when the target's branch rules dismiss stale ones, and webhooks get a merge_request event (synchronize); then its mergeability is checked again (check#MergeRequest), and it is merged when the target holds its head. For refresh#MergeRequests and propose#MergeRequest.

The framework's ref-update gitECA rule (Git.gitecas.xml): a branch moved. Each open merge request whose source it is, in this repository or in another of the fork network (sourceRepositoryId), takes the branch's head as it is now, whatever the event's newId (sync#MergeRequest), and each whose target it is is checked for mergeability again, and is merged when the target holds its head. One that fails is logged and the others are still refreshed.

A merge_request event of a merge request (opened, updated, ready, reviewed, synchronize, closed, reopened, merged) to the repository's webhooks. Nothing is sent of a hidden one (its title, text and head stay with the application); the service still runs, so the rules on it do. A failure is logged; the change it reports stands. Needs update on the merge request's repository, or authorization disabled (as the merge request services and an application call it): an event is signed with each webhook's secret.
